rules.problem: Omits 'age > 65' from the 'immunocompromised or at risk of severe disease' bullet, so an over-65 with suspected mpox isn't flagged urgent. The HIV branch requires a raised viral load, which drops 'not on ART'. Urgent is justified by the 'Give urgent attention' heading.

summary: Most consequential: the urgent priority rule omits 'age > 65' and narrows 'HIV not on ART/virologically unsuppressed' to HIV AND raised viral load, so at-risk patients the page flags for urgent attention are missed. The possible-mpox rule loses its timing (the 21-day contact window is anchored to now rather than symptom onset; fever loses its 2-day lookback), and the page's 'all lesions look similar, mpox more likely' isn't encoded. Several differential rules drop distinguishing qualifiers (chickenpox stages of healing, measles and tick bite fever spread patterns, shingles band, honey-coloured crusts), and a few SNOMED choices have closer concepts (Exposure to monkeypox virus, Lesion of skin of face, Thirst finding, Eruption of skin).
